title: Console walkthrough: usage analytics & per-route cost breakdown - Meridian Finance
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Meridian through Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdown. Discussed hosted vs dedicated options, routing/fallbacks, caching/batching impacts on cost, and security/compliance concerns (VPC, KMS, audit logs). Agreed next steps: send detailed pricing SKUs, share SOC2 & VPC docs, schedule security deep-dive and a 2-week pilot for production-like benchmarks.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Meridian VP Product), Marcus Reed (Head of ML), Anjali Patel (Security)

Summary (auto): Console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Action items and follow-ups captured.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you carving out time. I'm Jordan Lee, account exec at Redwood Inference. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Laura: Good, thanks. Excited to see the console — we want to understand cost implications per feature.
[00:10] Marcus: Yup, we've got a few high-throughput routes, want to see p99 latency and token spend per route.
[00:15] Jordan: Great, that's exactly what we plan to cover — we'll walk through the usage analytics page, then per-route dashboards, and end with the cost breakdown + next steps. Priya will drive the console.
[00:24] Priya: Cool, I'll share my screen. Sorry if the little bit of lag — network's fine on our end. Okay, so this is the Redwood Console home, top nav has Models, Routes, Analytics, Optimize. We'll go to Analytics first.
[00:35] [00:35] Priya: The main summary shows token usage trend by day, request count, and average latency. You can filter by model, route, or API key.
[00:42] Marcus: Can we filter by environment? staging vs prod?
[00:45] Priya: Yes — there's an environment tag on every route, and you can slice by that. Quick note: samples here are anonymized unless you enable debug mode.
[00:54] Laura: I'm interested in per-feature cost. We have chat, summarization, and rerank routes. How do we map those to dollars?
[01:02] Priya: Jumping to per-route dashboards — here's our route view. Each route has its own dashboard: traffic, token breakdown (prompt vs completion), latency percentiles, error rates, and importantly cost attribution.
[01:12] [01:12] Priya: Cost is broken down to token-level plus infra uplift. The console shows estimated token cost (model unit price * tokens) and then an infra charge that is a function of execution time and dedicated capacity if applicable.
[01:24] Marcus: Err — is infra uplift per-request or per-minute of GPU usage? How do you handle batching?
[01:30] Priya: Good question. Infra uplift is calculated per GPU-minute for Dedicated and as a share for Hosted. Batching reduces per-token infra cost by increasing GPU utilization; the dashboard has a 'batch efficiency' metric that shows effective tokens/sec on the backend.
[01:43] [01:43] Priya: There's also a knob in Optimize (we'll demo briefly) that recommends batching config and cache TTLs based on route patterns.
[01:50] Laura: And caching — KV cache? We want to cache prefixes for chat history to save cost — how is that surfaced?
[01:56] Priya: We support prefix/KV caching. On the route dashboard you'll see cache hit ratio and estimated savings if you enable prefix caching. The simulated savings tool will show both latency and dollar savings. Note: sometimes transcriptions or docs show 'K V cache' — sorry to be messy — but it's the same concept.
[02:10] Marcus: Nice. For our reranker pipeline which does many short requests, caching won't help, but batching might.
[02:16] Priya: Exactly, rerankers often benefit from micro-batching. The Optimize tab gives a suggested batch size and expected latency trade-off curve.
[02:23] [02:23] Jordan: Quick interjection — we typically recommend a split: keep latency-sensitive routes on a lower batch size or Dedicated with burst capacity, and throughput routes on larger batch sizes.
[02:33] Anjali: From security standpoint we need to know: VPC/private deployment options, KMS for key management, audit logs retention. Can you show where those appear?
[02:40] Priya: Sure — in the Console under Settings > Security we show KMS integrations, SSO/SAML config, and audit log settings. For Private deployments you get a customer-managed control plane and full audit logs with S3 sink.
[02:52] [02:52] Priya: We also store per-token traces for debugging if enabled, but by default payloads are redacted; audit logs are tamper-evident and tied to SIEM integrations.
[03:03] Anjali: Do you have SOC 2 certs? Also, can we get a copy of your audit policy?
[03:06] Jordan: Yes — we're SOC 2 Type II compliant, and we'll share the security pack after the call. We'll attach KMS docs and our VPC deployment checklist.
[03:14] Laura: Back to costs — can you show an example cost breakdown for a sample route?
[03:18] Priya: Sure — opening an example route 'chat-account-summary'. Here you can see hourly token usage, tokens per call, average completion length, and cost per route.
[03:27] [03:27] Priya: This chart shows that prompt tokens are 70% of spend; completion tokens are 30%. We also show a 'cost per 1k requests' estimate and historical trending.
[03:35] Marcus: Does that assume a specific model and quantization? We sometimes switch model families mid-rollout.
[03:40] Priya: The console ties cost to the actual model variant used. If you have routing policies that fallback to smaller models during congestion, you'll see blended cost. There's a column for model profile, including quantization level.
[03:52] [03:52] Priya: For example this route is served by 'rw-3b-quant' in normal times and 'rw-3b-8q' when latency allows — the cost diff is shown.
[03:59] Laura: How do rollouts appear? If we do a canary on 5% traffic, can we compare cost and quality?
[04:05] Priya: Yes — Routes > Rollouts shows traffic split, cost delta, and quality regressions (we can wire up your evals). You can roll back automatically if metric thresholds are breached.
[04:15] [04:15] Jordan: On the pricing model — hosted is usage-based; Dedicated has reserved GPU minutes + lower token unit price. We'll send a sample SKU sheet.
[04:23] Marcus: For Dedicated, do we get preemptible? We need predictable throughput for trading windows.
[04:28] Priya: Dedicated is reserved capacity with configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. There's also regional routing to keep latency consistent.
[04:36] Anjali: For procurement we need an on-prem option — can Redwood run entirely in our VPC, air-gapped?
[04:41] Jordan: We have Private deployments: control plane can be customer-managed and we do an on-prem package for regulated environments. We'll share the architecture diagram.
[04:49] [04:49] Laura: Could you demo the per-route SLA/alerting? We want alerts when cost per request spikes unexpectedly.
[04:55] Priya: Sure — under Alerts you can set thresholds on cost-per-request, token spikes, and latency SLOs. Alerts map to Slack, PagerDuty, or email and include drill-down links into the route dashboard.
[05:07] Marcus: Any examples of real customers using the cost alerts to catch regressor prompts?
[05:11] Priya: Yeah — a retail customer caught a runaway prompt that increased completion length by 4x; the cost alerts flagged it and auto-fallback to a cheaper model kept costs from spiraling.
[05:20] [05:20] Laura: Regarding billing granularity, will we get token-level line items in the invoice?
[05:25] Jordan: Invoices include per-route and per-model breakdowns; we can also provide a raw usage export (CSV) with token-level granularity by API key for internal chargebacks.
[05:34] Anjali: How long is usage export retained? For audit we need 12 months of retention.
[05:38] Priya: Standard retention is 6 months, extended retention is available as an add-on — we can include that in the pricing pack. Audit logs are separate and can be exported to your S3 for indefinite retention.
[05:50] [05:50] Marcus: Quick technical — in a Dedicated pool how do you handle KV cache affinity? We saw stale KV behavior on another provider.
[05:56] Priya: We pin KV cache to the serving slice and manage cache invalidation via TTLs; for high-consistency paths you can configure sticky routing to a slice. We'll share the cache design doc.
[06:06] Jordan: Let's talk timeline — Marcus mentioned wanting to pilot before EOY?
[06:10] Marcus: Ideally yes, small pilot next month to measure p99 and cost per route.
[06:15] Jordan: Great — proposed pilot: 2 weeks, mirror prod traffic for 3 priority routes. We'll provide a cost projection and a test harness.
[06:22] [06:22] Laura: Who will own instrumentation on our side? We'll need an engineer to set up API keys and route tagging.
[06:27] Marcus: I can own that. We'll provide traffic profiles and sample test keys.
[06:30] Anjali: Procurement also needs SOC2 and encryption docs — I'll prepare a list of must-haves.
[06:35] Priya: We'll attach SOC2, KMS integration guide, VPC checklist, and the architecture diagram after call.
[06:41] [06:41] Jordan: Cool, let's pause for questions from Marcus.
[06:44] Marcus: On the console, is there a way to project monthly cost if we change batching or model across routes?
[06:49] Priya: Yes, under Optimize there's a 'what-if' simulator — change model and batch settings and it projects monthly spend and latency percentiles. It uses your traffic profile if uploaded.
[06:59] Marcus: Can it simulate rollouts? Example 10% to new model and then scale up?
[07:03] Priya: Yes — you can simulate traffic splits and see blended cost/latency.
[07:09] Laura: Any limitations around data residency? Our customers in EU require EU-only data storage.
[07:14] Jordan: We support region pinning; with Private or Dedicated you can keep data in a specific region. We'll add region mapping to the docs we send.
[07:22] [07:22] Anjali: Also curious — do you capture PII in logs? We need to know redaction behavior.
[07:27] Priya: By default payloads are redacted, but you can enable structured logging with PII filters; for compliance we recommend routing logs to your S3 and applying your classification pipeline.
[07:38] Marcus: One more — how are regression alerts tied to evals? We have prompt sets.
[07:42] Priya: You can upload eval prompt sets and define quality metrics; the console will surface regression alerts when output quality drops after a rollout.
[07:50] [07:50] Jordan: Alright, quick recap of next steps then we'll hand off to security scheduling.
[07:55] Jordan: We'll send pricing SKUs and sample billing calc (Jordan), Priya will share dashboard exports and the caching design doc, and Marcus will provide traffic profiles and three priority routes. Anjali will send the compliance checklist.
[08:10] Anjali: Sounds good; I'll set up a follow up for the security deep-dive next week.
[08:15] Laura: One final note — can you give a brief on support levels? We'll likely go Dedicated if SLA and support are strong.
[08:20] Jordan: We have tiered support, enterprise includes a named CSM, 24/7 on-call for incidents, and a dedicated escalation path. We'll include support options in the pricing pack.
[08:30] [08:30] Priya: Wrapping up — I'll drop links here: demo workspace, cache design doc, and optimize recommendations. Also sample invoice export.
[08:39] Marcus: Perfect — thanks both.
[08:42] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack by Tuesday.
[08:46] Laura: Thanks.
[08:47] End

Notes: occasional small transcription errors (e.g., 'K V cache' instead of 'KV cache'), speaker labels may shift in a few places, natural filler words present. Links referenced during call: https://redwood.ai/docs/console-analytics (example), https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (example), demo workspace link (shared in chat).
